correctness.rationale: Acuaviva's Walsh eigenvalue formula gives the Schatten sum exactly. Singleton eigenvalues plus Kakutani's product-measure criterion prove that finite Schatten membership forces absolute continuity of every positive-time product measure and hence representability of the resolvent convolution. Level counting for exp(c j^gamma) gives the sharp subcritical, supercritical and geometric thresholds; cumulative multiplicities give the endpoint weak-Schatten law. Grouping geometric levels and applying an Abel limit gives the spectral-zeta residue, with the dyadic Hurwitz-zeta case providing an exact consistency check.

originality.rationale: Acuaviva supplies the general biased-sign resolvent and its Walsh spectrum but does not analyze Schatten ideals. Schachermayer's 1986 singular S_p example was inspected and uses direct product convolution with multiplicative eigenvalues, not the reciprocal-additive resolvent spectrum here. Searches by biased-sign resolvent, Walsh multiplier, Schatten, subset-sum spectrum, weak-Schatten and spectral-zeta formulations found no prior statement of the incompatibility theorem or the stated phase diagram. Classical product-measure, diagonalization and trace-ideal facts are excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp ideal-theoretic boundary hidden in a current L1 construction: its singular compact Schur resolvents lie outside every finite Schatten class. It also realizes arbitrary critical weak-Schatten exponents and provides an explicit spectral-zeta residue for geometric weights, clarifying the contrast with classical singular Schatten convolution examples.
